transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-11-17 15:00 PST
Duration: ~48 mins
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood Sec PM); Dr. Amrita, Jordan, Priya, Sandeep (Lyonesse)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on Lyonesse's requirements for an 'islanded' on-prem Redwood deployment: no outbound network, manually staged updates, strict signed artifacts, HSM/KMS integration for keys, and an expectation of a 99.5% inference availability within local clinic hours. They want a clear offline update story (USB or air-gapped staging node) plus a maintenance/rollback playbook. Cost sensitivity around long tail of underutilized GPUs and staffing for patching.

Topics Covered:
- Current infra inventory and patch cadence
- Update/patch process in airgapped environments
- Image signing, attestations, and KMS/HSM options
- Model pinning, rollbacks, and canary strategies for islanded clusters
- Expected throughput / latency SLOs and batching tradeoffs
- Support and on-call model for private deployments

Action items (briefed above)

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for carving out time today appreciate it. quick intro: my name's Maya, AE on the account — with me is Ethan on the technical side and Lina from security.
[00:12] Dr. Amrita (Lyonesse): hi all, thanks. we run clinical imaging analysis in a sealed cluster across our hospital partners so this is pretty high stakes.
[00:20] Ethan (Redwood): great, can you sketch your current environment — especially network egress and how you do updates today?
[00:27] Jordan (Lyonesse): sure. basically no outbound internet from the compute floor. we have a staging DMZ two racks over that has controlled USB import into a validation node. security team approves artifacts via comms with GRC, then Sandeep pushes to the island.
[00:39] Sandeep (Lyonesse): we currently use signed VM images from vendor X, and firmware is updated quarterly after regulatory review. patches are on a slow cadence.
[00:48] Priya (Lyonesse): also want audit trails for every change, chain-of-custody logs — we need to show inspectors.
[00:55] Lina (Redwood): understood; Redwood Private supports signed releases and we can integrate with HSM or customer KMS for key storage. can you tell us what HSM you use?
[01:05] Jordan: we have an on-prem Thales HSM and also AWS CloudHSM in our DR site but the compute island can't talk externally. so any signing must be done in the staging DMZ or by an offline operator.
[01:15] Ethan: we have two update patterns we've implemented before: one is an airgapped signed artifact that you bring to the island and a local validator verifies the signature against a pinned public key. second is a staging node that validates and then distributes via internal queue. both support rollback manifests.
[01:30] Dr. Amrita: show me the failure modes — if an update fails mid-apply what happens to long running KV caches and the model versions in flight?
[01:38] Ethan: good question. our runtime maintains per-request KV caching persisted to local disk in a write-ahead log so if a process dies mid-update the existing runtime can either continue serving with the previous model binary or we do an orchestrated drain then switch. for islanded setups we recommend a staged switch: start a parallel process with the new artifact, replay a controlled subset of traffic, then point the router. rollback is a one-command revert referencing the previous manifest.
[01:58] Jordan: the replay sounds heavy — we don't want latency blips in clinic hours.
[02:03] Maya: totally — that's why we talk about maintenance windows, and canaries outside clinic hours. what are your hours?
[02:08] Dr. Amrita: 7am to 8pm local; weekends limited staff.
[02:12] Maya: okay canaries would run 9pm to 4am then.
[02:16] Sandeep: about hardware — our racks are mixed: 2x H100 nodes, 4x A40-era cards, a couple older T4s used for lighter workloads. we also have BMC remote management but no internet.
[02:29] Ethan: that mix is workable. for the H100 we'd recommend full FP16+quant builds; for T4 we'd use lower perf quantized variants. Redwood's compilation step picks kernels based on GPU and sequence length distribution so we can supply optimized artifacts per SKU.
[02:45] Priya: how does licensing and support work? if an H100 fails do you replace binaries or do we bring replacement hardware?
[02:52] Maya: Redwood doesn't provide hardware — support covers software availability and fast recovery workflows; we can offer runbook-driven assisted updates and priority support which includes a technician-guided restore. hardware procurement is on your side but we partner with integrators if you want a single-pane offer.
[03:09] Dr. Amrita: any auditing for who triggered an update, who signed it — chain-of-custody? we need immutable logs.
[03:17] Lina: yes we keep an append-only audit log for deployments, signatures, and operator IDs — can be forwarded to your SIEM or stored locally. for airgapped setups we can write the log to a tamper-evident file and also print a signed manifest for inspectors.
[03:32] Jordan: what about KMS key rotation — we have strict rotation windows and can't expose private keys to the island.
[03:38] Ethan: key rotation handled in staging — you rotate keys in the HSM in the DMZ, sign the new artifacts, and ship them physically. Redwood's validators only need the public verification key which you can pin on the island. we also support hardware-backed attestation if you want TPM-based verification.
[03:55] Sandeep: is there a way to do a zero-touch update if we trust your release channel? we prefer manual but want the option of automating in DR.
[04:02] Maya: you can choose fully manual, semi-automated via staging node, or automated internal distribution — for compliance most customers pick manual+audited.
[04:10] Dr. Amrita: latency: our inference P95 must be < 220ms for the cardiac pipeline at 4 concurrent streams. what's realistic?
[04:18] Ethan: with H100 and optimized kernels you should be sub 80–120ms depending on batch strategy. the variable is KV cache locality and prefix lengths — if you need persistent session affinity we can pin KV caches to GPUs to avoid cold starts.
[04:32] Jordan: concurrency we figure average 3–5 concurrent requests. cost is a big sensitivity: we don't want to overprovision three H100s idle most of the day.
[04:42] Ethan: for that we recommend a mixed pool: keep one H100 for peak and offload low priority/async workloads to T4s. Redwood's routing policy can send latency-sensitive requests to H100 and fall back to cheaper nodes for best-effort tasks. autoscaling inside an island is manual — you can spin up a node but provisioning hardware remains manual.
[05:00] Priya: about security tests — do you do signed SBOMs and reproducible builds? auditors ask for provenance.
[05:07] Lina: yes we support SBOM exports for each release, including hash manifests for model artifacts and the compilation toolchain. we can also provide build reproducibility notes and attestations.
[05:19] Sandeep: patch windows — our change board approves quarterly; how do emergency hotfixes work?
[05:24] Maya: Redwood supports hotfix channels; we can qualify a hotfix in the staging DMZ and then ship a signed artifact marked as emergency. you'll get a shorter SLAs for verification and we provide step-by-step rollback if something goes wrong.
[05:36] Dr. Amrita: curious about telemetry — we can't exfil logs. can we run Redwood Console in read-only mode locally?
[05:42] Ethan: the Private control plane can run in your VPC or in fully offline mode. for fully islanded setups we deploy a console appliance that stores metrics and traces locally. from there you can export summaries or snapshot artifacts for auditors. streaming to Redwood-hosted console is optional and off by default.
[05:59] Jordan: what's the installer — is it a container image, ISO, or both?
[06:03] Ethan: both. we provide signed container bundles and an ISO image for airgapped installs. the ISO contains the runtime, validators, and a minimal orchestration layer that runs the distribution and manifest verification.
[06:14] Sandeep: how large are model artifacts? shipping multiple variants could be tens of gigabytes, how have you handled physical transfer?
[06:21] Ethan: common approach is delta packages and layered artifacts: base runtime is static, models are layered deltas. we also support chunked transfer that can resume. many customers ship on encrypted NVMe cartridges with checksums and signed manifests.
[06:36] Priya: do you support role-based access control internally — we need separation between operators who can stage vs who can approve?
[06:43] Lina: yes RBAC is configurable; approval flows can be gated by policy that requires two approvers for production releases. we can export approval records for audits.
[06:54] Dr. Amrita: what's the expected operational burden for a 3-node cluster day-to-day?
[06:59] Maya: realistically 1 FTE for operations initially, then 0.2–0.5 FTE after automations and playbooks, depending on how much manual change you require. we also offer managed support options.
[07:12] Jordan: do you have references in regulated healthcare? we need at least two references that have done similar islanded installs.
[07:18] Maya: yes, we can share redacted reference letters; one is a regional imaging center, another is a pharma lab that runs sealed inference. I'll include contacts as redacted references in the follow-up.
[07:29] Sandeep: backup strategy — do we snapshot models and cache state?
[07:33] Ethan: yes we recommend nightly snapshots of model artifacts and periodic KV cache checkpoints. snapshots are signed and stored in an offline archive to preserve provenance.
[07:42] Priya: legal/regulatory — SOC2 isn't enough for auditors; do you support attestation packages for ISO 27001 and local healthcare regs?
[07:51] Lina: we can provide compliance artifacts, SOC2 reports, penetration test summaries, and a compliance pack tailored for healthcare audits. however final attestation in an islanded environment typically comes from your internal audit after review of the local logs and manifests.
[08:06] Dr. Amrita: encryption at rest — do you let us bring our own keys for disk encryption?
[08:12] Ethan: yes BYOK for disk and model encryption; we can integrate with your HSM/TDE solution to decrypt only in the isolated environment.
[08:20] Jordan: talk through a sample update flow end-to-end please — from build to apply.
[08:25] Ethan: quick sketch: 1) build/compile model in CI with reproducible toolchain + generate SBOM, 2) sign artifact with staging HSM key, 3) export signed artifact (and signed manifest + SBOM) to encrypted transport media, 4) ingest on staging validator node in DMZ, run offline validation tests, 5) operator approves in GRC system, 6) physically move media to island, run local manifest verification and dry-run, 7) schedule maintenance window, 8) perform staged rollout with canary then full cutover, 9) generate audit record and snapshot.
[08:53] Priya: dry-run step — can you simulate production load without external traffic?
[08:58] Ethan: yes we can replay recorded traces or run a synthetic load generator locally. we recommend a short synthetic replay during dry-run.
[09:07] Dr. Amrita: what about fallback models for degraded hardware?
[09:11] Ethan: Redwood supports model variants and automated fallback. if H100 unavailable, routing rules send to quantized A40 variant. decisioning is policy driven and you can set cost/latency priorities.
[09:22] Jordan: competitor question — we've heard OnPremX promises full automation in islands, is Redwood more hands-on?
[09:28] Maya: Redwood trades full automation for safety and auditability in these deployments. we give flexible automation but default to human-in-the-loop for production in regulated settings.
[09:36] Sandeep: network isolation concerns — do your validators require any outbound CRL/OCSP checks during signature verification?
[09:42] Ethan: no, signature verification is local and uses pinned CA certificates. CRL/OCSP can be optionally included but would require a local CRL cache you update during staging.
[09:51] Priya: what's your SLA for Private islanded support?
[09:54] Maya: standard private SLA is 99.5% uptime and a 4-hour P1 response; premium packages can get tighter response times.
[10:02] Dr. Amrita: curious about cost model — is this just software + support or commit to capacity?
[10:07] Maya: options: software license + support, or reserved capacity model if you want Redwood-managed hosted nodes. for islanded on-prem it's typically license + support plus an optional managed service bundle.
[10:18] Jordan: final question on backups — we want an immutable offline backup for at least two years as per regulation.
[10:24] Ethan: supported; we produce signed archives with retention metadata and you can store them in your offline vault.
[10:31] Maya: ok to recap next steps: Ethan will send the airgapped install checklist and image signing guide; I'll send pricing and references; Lyonesse to share hardware SKUs and maintenance windows; we'll schedule security deep dive.
[10:43] Dr. Amrita: thanks, that plan works for us.
[10:46] Priya: we'll get you the inventory by Monday.
[10:49] Maya: perfect, thanks all.
[10:52] Jordan: thanks everyone, bye.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription captured most content but some proper nouns may be garbled; technical terms double-checked during follow-up (e.g., exact Thales model, BMC firmware revisions).
